findings.namedBuyers: Two verified commercially relevant organizer contacts: Dr. Abbas Zavar, FHLIP Co-Chair and Executive Director, co-leading the conference since 2024; and Dr. Karim Keshavjee, FHLIP Co-Chair and EMHI Program Director. Zavar is the first relationship-development route for conference logistics; Keshavjee is particularly relevant to the associated residential teaching component. Their roles do not establish hotel contract or procurement authority. Official conference mailbox: ihpme.fhlip.conference@utoronto.ca. Keshavjee’s published programme email: karim.keshavjee@utoronto.ca. Michael Stead, MHI/EMHI Graduate Program Assistant, is a secondary operational routing contact at ihpme.mhi.program@utoronto.ca; hotel-buying responsibility is unverified.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming: February 19, 2027, in person, Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Official conference and registration pages both state 8:00 AM–5:00 PM EST. The tentative agenda additionally shows a sponsor reception until 7:00 PM; confirm reception timing separately. These are activity dates, not page-publication dates. No exact 2028 conference date or venue was found; the EMHI roadmap references required FHLIP attendance in winter 2028, which is not an edition announcement.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel specifications: Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown is a conditional city-hotel lodging prospect, not a resort or whole-conference replacement. The existing campus venue and historical 400+ attendance make the supplied approximately 240-theatre ballroom unsuitable for a full-event plenary at historical scale. A limited speaker/VIP/delegate allocation or non-local EMHI residency group is more realistic than exclusive housing. The published two 10-day academic residencies provide a stronger multi-night lead than the one-day conference alone, but February 2027 check-in/out dates, non-local cohort size and willingness to stay on Queens Quay are unverified. Do not translate course duration into room nights, assume 15–109 peak rooms, or classify this as relocation. Campus access rather than MTCC access is the location issue. Side meetings are only a proposal; no off-site requirement is published. Do not promise catering while the hotel’s restaurant/lounge status remains unresolved.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: University of Toronto Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College Street, Toronto, Ontario. Toronto proper, downtown university/College Street district; not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. This is a campus venue, not a competing hotel. Both the main location panel and Eventbrite agree. Caveat: the conference page still describes the Innovation Showcase as being on the second floor of Myhal Centre, and an earlier organizer announcement named Myhal. A later organizer announcement names Schwartz Reisman. Treat Schwartz Reisman as the primary published venue, but reconfirm whether the showcase text is stale or a second site. No signed venue contract was reviewed.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified Toronto campus progression: February 22, 2024 — Hart House, hybrid, 254 attendees (115 in person; 139 virtual); February 21, 2025 — Dalla Lana School of Public Health, 288 attendees (243 in person; 45 virtual); February 20, 2026 — Myhal Centre for Engineering Innovation and Entrepreneurship, with 400+ attendees reported on the conference retrospective. The 2025 retrospective headline says 300+, but the edition-specific report gives 288; prefer the detailed report. This is local campus venue change, not evidence of destination rotation or historical hotel commitments.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. No edition-specific host hotel, housing bureau, hotel list, room block, lodging booking link or open accommodation RFP was found in the official conference, registration or EMHI pages reviewed. Hotels listed for this edition: none found. This is not evidence that hotel sourcing is open or that no private arrangements exist. Registration says: “Join us for the fourth annual Future of Health Leadership, Informatics and Policy (FHLIP) Conference.” The programme provides a separate lodging-demand lead: “Students are required to be on campus for two residencies of 10 days each in February of Year 1 and February of Year 2.” EMHI details say the residential component is held in February “to synergize with the annual” FHLIP conference. These quotes establish an academic-residency connection, not a hotel booking commitment or ten hotel nights.
findings.organizationStructure: University-led academic conference presented by the University of Toronto Institute of Health Policy, Management and Evaluation (IHPME), growing out of its Master of Health Informatics programme within the Dalla Lana School of Public Health. Not established as an independent association, corporate event agency, PCO or DMC. Eventbrite provides registration; that does not make it the housing buyer. OntarioMD is Zavar’s professional affiliation, not evidence that it owns the event.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No incumbent hotel, contracted hotel inventory, housing-bureau restriction or demonstrated hotel overflow was identified. A sponsor reception is already in the tentative conference programme, so it is not an established off-site reception opportunity. Campus-based venues are the demonstrated meeting incumbents. The organizer anticipates another sold-out event, but limited conference seating is not evidence of sold-out guestrooms or hotel overflow. Inference: the hotel’s Harbourfront setting may require a less convenient campus journey than a campus-adjacent option; no competitor hotel commitment or travel-time comparison is asserted.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Abbas Zavar through ihpme.fhlip.conference@utoronto.ca and Karim Keshavjee at karim.keshavjee@utoronto.ca. Ask who coordinates speaker travel and February EMHI lodging, whether lodging is individual-paid or centrally arranged, and whether any hotel agreements already exist. Request the 2027 residential calendar, non-local headcount, actual room nights/peak rooms, budget and procurement route. Reconfirm Schwartz Reisman versus residual Myhal showcase references. Only if need is confirmed, offer a modest lodging allocation or a residency-length rate proposal with explicit campus-access arrangements; do not allocate speculative inventory or promise catering. Ask when the next annual accommodation review occurs. Leave qualification and publication decisions to ORS.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: February 2027 is a confirmed event within the requested horizon. The conference venue is already published elsewhere, so do not pitch replacement meeting space as an open requirement. Lodging accessibility remains unconfirmed, not closed and not verified open. Registration being open does not mean hotel sourcing is open. A short organizer qualification conversation is justified by the connected residential programme, but there is no qualified room block yet.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: cultivate an annual academic-residency accommodation relationship rather than assume a rotating full-conference hotel bid. Recurrence is explicit: Eventbrite calls 2027 the fourth annual conference; EMHI documents February residential teaching and the roadmap requires FHLIP attendance in winter 2028. This supports future-cycle relationship development, not an exact 2028 event date, venue or open hotel requirement. Historical campus venues do not establish a hotel procurement cycle.
